title: Unit of Work

validation.research: Six authoritative source notes. Fowler’s Unit of Work catalog entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes tracking affected objects and coordinating their persistence and concurrency policy. Percival and Gregory support scoped persistence and explicit completion. SQLAlchemy documentation distinguishes instrumented tracking, flushing, committing, and additional expected-version protection. Official SQLite and Python documentation supports the local transaction, BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention, explicit SQL configuration, and connection ownership. The article distinguishes the pattern from a generic transaction wrapper or job batch. The label scenario, manual tracker, code, and diagrams are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article fences execute as uow.py and demo.py with five stated output lines exactly. Checks cover explicit new/dirty/deleted tracking, no SQL during registration, update/insert/delete order, immutable snapshots, exact nonblank ASCII IDs and printable text boundaries, single final intent per ID, no-commit discard and exception cleanup, duplicate registration, wrong object types, later-insert failure and missing-row rollback after an earlier update, single-use lifecycle, preservation of a pre-existing caller transaction, exception after successful commit, empty commit, quoted IDs, explicit connection configuration, actual competing SQLite writers, committed visibility, closed connections, and stale proposals overwriting newer state. The latter explicitly demonstrates that a write lock acquired at commit does not provide expected-version protection for previously collected snapshots.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ and standard-library SQLite. Independent label rows, exact nonblank ASCII IDs, and 1–40 printable nonblank label characters. Explicit immutable snapshots classify one final intent per ID; registrations do not issue SQL. Explicit commit applies updates, inserts, and deletes under one local transaction, with IDs sorted within each group. Default exit discards unwritten proposals; an in-scope commit attempt or scope exit consumes the coordinator. Caller owns connection closing; the coordinator owns only the transaction it starts. Failed writes roll back earlier participating writes, while exceptions after successful commit cannot undo it. No automatic dirty tracking, identity map, repeated-intent coalescing, read API, foreign-key dependency ordering, version checks, authorization, automatic retry, or cross-resource coordination is implemented. Writer locking starts at commit, so stale proposals can still overwrite newer values.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
